title: Bananas (per lb)

adjustment.analysis: No events, promotions, or price changes are scheduled. The baseline already reflects recent trends and seasonal patterns (e.g., back-to-school season). The Labor Day week (2026-09-07) saw a dip to 241 units (vs baseline 437.1), but this was due to a holiday and is already accounted for in the baseline's recent history. No promotion or price change is active. The classical uplift model confirms no expected lift. The baseline’s median is well-calibrated, and the 30% ordinary-week noise suggests that past fluctuations are within normal variation. No driver justifies a multiplier adjustment.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-30% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
